name: Value of taxable supply
definition: The value of a supply is the transaction value — the price actually paid or payable for the supply — but only where the supplier and recipient are not related and the price is the sole consideration. To that value s.15(2) ADDS other statutory levies charged separately, amounts the supplier was liable for but the recipient incurred, incidental expenses including commission and packing, interest, late fee or penalty for delayed payment, and subsidies directly linked to the price other than Central and State Government subsidies. s.15(3) EXCLUDES a discount recorded in the invoice at or before the supply, and a post-supply discount only where it was agreed at or before the supply, linked to specific invoices, and the recipient has reversed the attributable input tax credit. Where s.15(1) cannot apply, s.15(4) sends the valuation to the prescribed manner.
why_it_exists: It fixes the AMOUNT on which GST is charged. s.9(1) levies the tax on the value determined under s.15, so an error here is an error in the tax itself, not a presentation matter. The dangerous half is s.15(2): amounts a bookkeeper would naturally treat as recoveries or as finance income — packing, commission, interest on late payment — are part of the taxable base.

common_mistakes: taking the invoice total as the value without adding the s.15(2) inclusions
excluding packing and commission as recoveries — s.15(2)(c) includes them
treating interest on late payment as finance income outside GST — s.15(2)(d) includes it in the value
excluding a post-supply discount before the recipient has reversed the attributable input tax credit — s.15(3)(b)(ii) makes that reversal a condition
excluding a pre-supply discount that was never recorded in the invoice — s.15(3)(a) makes the invoice record a condition
using transaction value for a supply to a director or an employee — they are related persons under the s.15 Explanation
assuming GST is charged on GST — the four GST Acts are carved out of s.15(2)(a); other statutory levies are not
dependencies: UNKNOWN — CGST Rules valuation provisions referred to by s.15(4) and s.15(5) not extracted
UNKNOWN — the list of supplies notified under s.15(5) is not held locally

icai_references: NOT APPLICABLE — the value of a taxable supply is a statutory computation under s.15. It is not the accounting measurement of revenue, and the two amounts can differ on the same transaction
gst_references: CGST Act, 2017 s.15(1) to s.15(5), the Explanation to s.15(2), and the Explanation to s.15 defining related persons
evidence_required: the tax invoice, with every separately charged line
the agreement, where a discount or a non-price consideration is claimed
for a post-supply discount: the pre-supply agreement, the linkage to specific invoices, and the document evidencing the recipient's input tax credit reversal
the relationship between supplier and recipient
for subsidies: who provided the subsidy and whether it is directly linked to the price
confidence_factors: weak when only the invoice is held — s.15(2)(b) and s.15(3)(b) both turn on facts that never appear on it
weak when the relationship between the parties is unknown, because s.15(1) is conditional on it
zero for a post-supply discount until the recipient's input tax credit reversal is evidenced
zero where s.15(4) or s.15(5) applies — the prescribed rules are not held locally
validation_checks: every s.15(2) inclusion has been considered before the value is fixed
a discount is excluded only under s.15(3)(a) or s.15(3)(b), never because it appears in the accounts
a post-supply discount is excluded only on evidence of the recipient's input tax credit reversal
a related-party supply is NOT valued at transaction value under s.15(1)
the value used for GST is recorded separately from the amount recognised as revenue in the books
examples: unrelated parties, price the sole consideration, packing charged separately — the value is the price plus the packing charge under s.15(2)(c)
a discount agreed before the supply and shown on the face of the invoice — excluded under s.15(3)(a)
counterexamples: a year-end volume rebate issued by credit note where no pre-supply agreement exists — s.15(3)(b)(i) is not satisfied, so the value of supply is unchanged and the rebate does not reduce the GST
goods supplied to an employee at cost — employer and employee are related persons under the s.15 Explanation, so s.15(1) does not apply and the transaction value is not the taxable value
